follow100Note: AWS alone earned $9.4B of operating profit — 62% of Amazon's total — on just $17.47 of every $100 of sales. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
oneTimers: A $2.0B pre-tax paper loss on Amazon's common-stock investment in Rivian Automotive sits inside non-operating expense — it is a revaluation of shares Amazon owns, not money lost to customers. A year ago the same line held a $0.5B loss.
otherDetail: Interest income $993M, less $644M interest expense and $2,673M of other expense, net — the non-operating lines include a $2.0B pre-tax valuation loss on Amazon's stake in Rivian; an $85M equity-method loss is recorded below the tax line.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Stores, subscriptions and ads in North America — the biggest piece, and it earned a $5.0B operating profit, up from $0.9B a year ago.

segments.name: International
segments.note: The same businesses outside North America — swung to a $0.9B operating profit after a $1.2B loss a year earlier.

segments.name: AWS
segments.note: Cloud computing rented to other companies — grew 17%, and its $9.4B operating profit was 62% of Amazon's total.

takeaways.text: AWS sales grew 17% to $25.0B — a $100B annual revenue run rate, per CEO Andy Jassy — and the segment earned $9.4B of operating profit at a 37.6% margin, 62% of Amazon's total, as companies renewed infrastructure modernization and bought AI work on its cloud.
takeaways.title: AWS reaccelerated

takeaways.text: Consolidated operating income rose 221% from a year ago: North America earned $5.0B (up from $0.9B) and International swung from a $1.2B loss to a $0.9B profit as the store networks got more efficient.
takeaways.title: Operating income more than tripled

takeaways.text: Net income rose to $10.4B from $3.2B a year ago even though $2.0B of it was wiped out by a paper loss on Amazon's investment in electric-truck maker Rivian, recorded before tax. Free cash flow over the trailing twelve months swung to a $50.1B inflow from a $3.3B outflow.
takeaways.title: Profit tripled despite the Rivian drag

verdict: Amazon's sales rose 13% to $143.3B and operating income more than tripled to $15.3B as AWS reaccelerated to 17% growth and International turned profitable — and it kept $10.4B as profit even after a $2.0B paper loss on its Rivian stake.
